title: PILOT-2 ben2 -- L5': the numerical basis of S_2(Gamma') (dim 4), the dimension scan, the held-out design inside the narrow band, and the 1/9 structure gate
author: mathematician (Opus 5)

spec.precedence: ruling 1801: ben1's certified machine values override the spec's printed literals

target.member_discrimination: NOT done here. The dimension fingerprint (4,9,15,21,27) is an arithmetic progression shared by all 6 members, and the 1/9 lacunarity of [G4'-e] depends only on Delta(9,9,9) and the order-9 expansion point, which every member shares. Member identification is ben1's [G1'-f] group-theoretic assert (spec sec.4.2 / E-11).

conventions.normalisation: f(z) = (1-w)^k sum_n b_n w^n , b_n = btilde_n/rho^n , w=(z-p)/(z-conj p), p=z_a=i
conventions.expansion_point: p = z_a = i (Gamma'-regular: sigma_0 is a 9-cycle)
conventions.VW_machinery: Voight-Willis (1),(4),(9),(11) + Rmk 3.4 rescaling, transcribed from PILOT-1 scratchpad/pilot1_ben4_L5_linalg.jl

part_G4a_heldout_design.answer_to_ben1_U-B2: YES -- a structurally separated held-out set fits inside the narrow band (inradius, rho] = (0.8294934, 0.9377554].  The separation is imposed on three coordinates at once.

separation_1_radius.why_largest: the held-out shell sits at 0.99950*rho, OUTSIDE every fit shell, so the held-out test is an EXTRAPOLATION to the hardest radius (largest truncation error ~ |w|^(N+1), closest to the FD boundary), not an interpolation.  This is the strongest placement available.
separation_1_radius.exactness: the radii are distinct as exact BigFloat values => no held-out point is a fit point (structural and exact, the PILOT-1 ben4 argument)

separation_2_angle.note: each fit shell uses its own offset; the held-out shell uses a different offset and a different (prime) point count

part_G4a_heldout_design.separation_3_reading: distinct |w| does NOT by itself exclude Gamma'-equivalence (Gamma' does not preserve |w|), so the two REDUCED point clouds were compared directly.  Minimum hyperbolic distance held-out<->fit = 6.6336e-03, versus 2.6522e-02 for the nearest-neighbour spacing INSIDE the fit cloud: the held-out relations are not Gamma'-translates of fit relations, but the margin is only ~4x the intrinsic spacing and is reported, not idealised.
part_G4a_heldout_design.trivial_row_note: measured trivial fractions are exact multiples of 1/18 of the sampled directions (0%, 5%=18/360, 10%=36/360), which independently reproduces the 18-fold dihedral symmetry of the regular 18-gon fundamental domain that ben1 certified.

residual_over_truncation_scale.reading: the held-out residual tracks the VW truncation scale rho^(N+1) with a multiplier of 327 (N=538) and 2.7e+03 (N=717), i.e. the residual is truncation-limited, not arithmetic-limited (256-bit working precision is ~1e-77).

part_G4b_dimension_scan.riemann_roch_table_source: scratchpad/pilot2_ben2_i_rrtable_out.json (emitted by the same code the gates use; deg L_k = (k/2)(2g-2) + sum floor((k/2)(1-1/e_i)), dim = deg - g + 1 when non-special)
part_G4b_dimension_scan.fingerprint_weakness: PRE-REGISTERED (spec sec.4.2): the fingerprint is the arithmetic progression 4,9,15,21,27 and does NOT discriminate the 6 passport members -- all six give the same numbers. This scan tests only whether the numerical basis is the real thing.

part_G4c_rank_gap.two_detectors: two rank detectors are reported for every weight. (D1) threshold (PILOT-1 ben4 verbatim, cut at 1e-3 * leading pivot) presupposes an empty band at that level and FAILS for k>=8 here, where the spectrum decays smoothly through 1e-3.  (D2) largest single drop in the pivot-norm sequence is level-free.  D2 was introduced AFTER D1 was seen to fail at k=8 -- declared post-hoc.  'all_match' below uses D2.
part_G4c_rank_gap.finding: the PILOT-1 threshold detector (cut at 1e-3 of the leading pivot) is NOT transferable to this target at higher weight.  It reproduces the prediction for k = [2, 4, 6] and FAILS for k = [8, 10], where the pivot-norm spectrum decays smoothly through 1e-3 and only drops at a much lower level.  The level-free largest-gap detector reproduces the prediction at EVERY weight, with the drop unique and separated from the runner-up ratio by a factor between 3.13e+04 and 3.99e+07.
part_G4c_rank_gap.honesty: the largest-gap detector was introduced AFTER the threshold detector was seen to fail at k=8.  Both are reported for every run; no run was discarded.  The first k=8/k=10 attempts (at N=300, where the threshold detector returned dim 45 and 112 against the predictions 21 and 27) are kept in all_runs above.

N=538.theta3_applicability: NOT APPLICABLE to the VW relation matrix. W3 is a ben4 gate on the Sym^2 / Sym^3 monomial coefficient matrices, whose columns have comparable norms. Two features of the VW matrix make a condition-number cap of that shape unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION: (i) column n carries (w/rho)^n and (w'/rho)^n, so the column norms decay geometrically in n; (ii) on the outermost sample shell the reduction barely moves the point, so w' is close to w and the two terms of the row nearly cancel at large n. Neither is a degeneracy of the SOLUTION. The independent evidence that the surviving side is healthy is elsewhere in this cert: the held-out residual, the agreement of the N=538 and N=717 runs on the leading coefficients, and the size and uniqueness of the rank gap. Recorded for completeness, NOT read as a gate.

spec_sec6_W3_style_thresholds.scope_note: W3 is a ben4 retreat condition defined on the Sym^2/Sym^3 matrices.  These are the ANALOGOUS numbers for the ben2 VW relation matrix, recorded because ruling 1801 asks for them. theta1/theta2/theta4 transfer and PASS at both N; theta3 (condition-number cap) does not transfer -- see its applicability note.

part_G4c_rank_gap.float64_svd_caveat: Float64 svdvals are reported for reference only; the downcast caps the observable range at ~1e-16, so the true kernel level is visible ONLY in the BigFloat pivot-norm sequence (which interlaces the singular values).
part_G4c_rank_gap.key_naming_warning: in the run JSONs the key 'cond_s1_over_sr' actually stores sigma_r / sigma_1 (the surviving side's level relative to the leading pivot), NOT sigma_1 / sigma_r. The theta3 entry above reports the reciprocal, i.e. the genuine condition number sigma_1/sigma_r.

truncation_vs_weight.observation: the truncation N needed to expose the kernel grows with the weight k.  At N=300 the largest-gap ratio falls monotonically with k (see gap_ratio_at_N300_by_weight); raising N to 460 restores it for k=8 and k=10 (see gap_ratio_at_N460_by_weight).
truncation_vs_weight.candidate_explanation: for a weight-k form on a cocompact group, |f| Im(z)^(k/2) is bounded, so in the disk the VW series behaves like (1-|w|)^(-k/2) and its coefficients grow like n^(k/2-1). The truncation residual then scales like N^(k/2-1) * |w|^(N+1) rather than |w|^(N+1).  This matches the observed cliff between k=6 and k=8 at N=300.  GRADE: candidate (a heuristic fit to 5 data points), NOT proved here.

part_G4d_precision.attained_D_definition: D := -log10(max over the 61 held-out points and over all basis vectors of the relative automorphy defect |f(w') - j^k f(w)| / max(|f(w')|,|j^k f(w)|))
part_G4d_precision.spec_floor_check: spec sec.6 W3 refuses to evaluate its thresholds when D < 12.  D = 16.61 at N=717 (and 12.53 already at N=538), so ben4 may proceed.

coefficient_stability_production_N538_vs.reading: the first 20 rescaled coefficients of each of the four basis vectors agree between the two independent production runs to this level; the two runs share the sampling design but not the matrix, the truncation, or the linear algebra trajectory.

echelon_pivots.note: pivots (0,1,2,3) are machine output, not chosen by hand (spec sec.1.4)

part_G4d_precision.basis_note: b_n = btilde_n / rho^n ; f(z) = (1-w)^2 sum_n b_n w^n ; only n = 0..19 are exported here, the full N=717 vectors live in scratchpad/pilot2_ben2_g_prod_k2N717_out.json

part_G4e_structure.prediction_source: spec sec.4.2 [G-4'-e] (pre-registered): dim M_6(Delta(9,9,9)) = 1; that line sits inside the 15-dimensional S_6(Gamma'); expanded at the order-9 elliptic point p = z_a it has b_n = 0 unless n = -k/2 = 6 (mod 9).  NO input from Delta enters the computation -- the whole run sees only Gamma'.

measured_k6_N538.verdict: EXACTLY 1 of the 15 echelon basis vectors is lacunary: pivot n in [6], dominant class 6 mod 9, ratio (max off-class / max in-class) = 2.869e-14.  The other 14 vectors have ratios 0.638 to 0.998.  Prediction (pivot 6, residue 6, count 1) CONFIRMED.

second_instance_k8_N460.status: derived from the SAME spec formula and written down BEFORE the k=8 basis was computed (scratchpad/pilot2_ben2_i_rrtable_out.json)
second_instance_k8_N460.verdict: EXACTLY 2 of the 21 echelon basis vectors are lacunary, with pivots n in [5, 14], both in class 5 mod 9, ratios ['9.014e-10', '2.564e-09'].  Predicted pivots [5, 14], predicted residue 5, predicted count 2 = dim M_8(Delta).  A second, independent instance of the same mechanism with a DIFFERENT residue class and a DIFFERENT multiplicity.  Non-lacunary ratios run 0.632 to 0.982.

part_G4e_structure.sharpening_with_N: the lacunarity ratio tracks the truncation floor: 1.147e-08 at N=300 (floor rho^301 = 3.972e-09) and 2.869e-14 at N=538 (floor rho^539 = 9.042e-16), i.e. the off-class coefficients are zero to the accuracy the run can see, not merely small.
part_G4e_structure.control: at k=2 and k=4 the Riemann-Roch table gives dim M_k(Delta(9,9,9)) = 0, so NO basis vector should be lacunary -- and none is (k=2 ratios 0.734 to 0.941 at N=717).
part_G4e_structure.comparison_to_PILOT1: PILOT-1 saw 1/3 lacunarity at an order-3 elliptic point; this is 1/9, three times sparser, and it appears twice (k=6 and k=8) with the residue class shifting as -k/2 mod 9.
part_G4e_structure.does_not_discriminate_members: this gate is an INPUT-FREE structure check, not a member discriminator: Delta(9,9,9) and the order-9 expansion point are shared by all 6 members (spec sec.4.2 / E-11).

part_G4f_controls.delta_a_membership_check: Gamma' is the stabiliser of coset 1 and sigma_a(1) != 1, so delta_a moves coset 1 and lies outside Gamma' (exact integer check in the control script)
part_G4f_controls.reading: MU-A' (j^k -> j^{-k}) turns dim 4 into 11 (k=2) and dim 15 into 33 (k=6), with the rank gap collapsing to 1.25 and 1.8 (no rank gap at all).  MU-B' (gamma -> gamma*delta_a) turns them into 0 and 1.  The baseline reproduces the prediction (4, 15) in the same script.  The G-4' dimension gate is therefore not vacuous.
part_G4f_controls.MU4_reading: mixing the held-out shell into the fit lowers the held-out residual from 7.413e-03 to 9.420e-04 (factor 7.87) at N=160.  The collapse is real but modest at this N because the residual there is truncation-limited rather than fit-limited; the point stands that the separation must be structural, which it is (disjoint exact radii).

rrqr_equivalence.why: the production runs use rrqr_fast, which skips already-pivoted columns and downdates the column norms with an exact refresh every 25 steps.  Both are exact optimisations, but the certified code path is ben1/PILOT-1's rrqr_ref, so equivalence was demonstrated before use.
rrqr_equivalence.result: identical pivot sequences, identical pivot norms to 0 relative difference, identical ranks, identical echelon bases to 5.18e-75, on 3 probes (k=2 N=100, k=2 N=160, k=6 N=120).  Speedup 2.16x to 2.46x.

checkpointing.why: spec sec.7.4 / ruling 1801: local background runs are killed without warning after 10-12 minutes, so a single invocation must stay well inside that.
checkpointing.scheme: the modified Gram-Schmidt runs under a wall-clock budget, serialises its entire working state (C, R, pivots, pivot norms, used flags, downdated norms, step counter) with Julia Serialization, and exits; re-invocation resumes at the same step.  The arithmetic is bit-identical to an uninterrupted run because the state is complete.
checkpointing.budget_bound: every invocation's MGS phase was capped by the budget argument above (max 245 s), so no single Julia process ran more than about 5 minutes including build and finish -- well inside the 10-12 minute kill window measured for background runs.
checkpointing.the_D20_run_needed: 4 invocations for N=717 (825.7 s of MGS in total)

heldout_defect_outlier_diagnostic.symptom: on the LACUNARY basis vectors (k=6 pivot 6; k=8 pivots 5 and 14) the maximum RELATIVE held-out defect is large (6.1e-02, 5.6e-01, 2.6e-01) while the median is ~1e-12 / ~1e-09.
heldout_defect_outlier_diagnostic.test: scratchpad/pilot2_ben2_h_defectdiag.jl re-measures at N=300 and reports, per point, both the relative defect and a globally scaled defect |lhs-rhs| / max over the held-out set of max(|lhs|,|rhs|).
heldout_defect_outlier_diagnostic.result: at the point achieving the relative maximum for the k=6 lacunary vector, max(|lhs|,|rhs|) = 2.855e-04 against a set maximum of 1.588e+01 (ratio 1.798e-05), i.e. the form is essentially VANISHING there; the globally scaled defect at that point is 5.620e-05, in line with the 5.66e-07..0.000193 of the non-lacunary k=6 vectors.  The inflation is a zero of the form, not a failure of automorphy.
heldout_defect_outlier_diagnostic.consequence: the headline attained-D of this cert is taken from the k=2 run, where no basis vector has this problem (max relative defect 2.461e-17 at N=717 across all four vectors).

cost_model_vs_ben1.note: ben1's extrapolation used its own row count (~0.91*(N+1) after trivial rejection) and the unoptimised rrqr; ben2 used more rows (see rows_ben2_over_Nplus1) and rrqr_fast.  The two effects nearly cancel.

W1_monitoring.what_it_counts: the sum of the build and MGS seconds that the runs themselves reported, over every ben2 run including the failed first attempts and the equivalence probes.  It excludes Julia process startup / JIT, which added roughly 10-25 s per invocation.
W1_monitoring.trigger_condition_from_dispatch: report immediately if the measurement exceeds 3x ben1's extrapolation

unknowns.text: The largest-gap rank detector was adopted after the threshold detector failed at k=8. It reproduces Riemann-Roch at every weight with a unique, hugely separated drop, but no a-priori bound on the runner-up ratio was proved; the detector is validated empirically (runner-up stays between 1.4 and 2.5 in every run) and not by theory.

The N^(k/2-1) * |w|^(N+1) truncation model that explains why higher weights need larger N is a candidate fitted to five data points, not a proof. It matters for ben4/ben5 only in that it predicts how N must grow if higher weights are ever needed.

The measured minimum hyperbolic distance between the held-out and fit REDUCED clouds (6.634e-03) is about 0.25x the nearest-neighbour spacing inside the fit cloud itself (2.652e-02); it certifies non-coincidence but the margin is modest, a direct consequence of how thin the usable band is. Widening it would require either a larger angular count or accepting fit shells further from rho (worse conditioning).

The relative held-out defect is not a good statistic on basis vectors that nearly vanish at a sample point (step H). ben4/ben5 should use the globally scaled defect if they measure residuals on the lacunary vectors.

Attained precision at N=717 is D = 16.61 digits, not the nominal D = 20 that N(D=20) = 717 was chosen for: the held-out residual sits about 2.7e+03 times the truncation scale rho^(N+1). If ben5's coefficient recognition needs more than about 17 digits, N must be raised; N(D) is linear in D (N = D*ln10 / -ln rho), so an ATTAINED D of 20 needs roughly N = 863.

grade: cross-checked in the internal sense only. The dimension fingerprint agrees with an independent Riemann-Roch computation; the two production runs (N=538, N=717) agree on the first 20 coefficients; rrqr_fast was shown bit-identical to ben1's certified rrqr_ref; the 1/9 lacunarity is an input-free structural prediction confirmed twice with different residues and multiplicities; two destructive controls break the gate. NOT a second independent implementation of the VW layer itself (both runs share pilot2_ben1_L4_core.jl and the same row construction). NOT verified: no Lean. NOT genuine: nothing here is a claim about GT-shadows.
